messages:
maria: Heads-up — saw a burst of DCGM alerts (ECC/Xid) in usw2 around 2766666200. ~40 alerts in ~10m, majority from a single node during kernel/driver churn. Thinking we should move from an instantaneous >0 alert to an adaptive windowed approach to reduce noise and avoid premature drains.

derek: Saw the same. Most were transient resets during driver probe. Our current prom rule fires on any xid > 0 in 1m which is too sensitive.

sasha: Can you paste the current / proposed rule? We have grouping by gpu_id but still get noisy paging.

maria: Proposed idea: compute a rolling increase over 5-10m as a recording rule then alert only when the windowed increase exceeds a small threshold AND persists. Example recording + alert (draft):

```yaml
# recording: per-card xid increase over 5m
record: gpu:xid:count_5m
expr: increase(dcgm_gpu_xid_errors_total[5m])
---
alert: GPUCardXidPersistent
expr: gpu:xid:count_5m > 3
for: 10m
labels:
  severity: page
annotations:
  summary: 'gpu {{ $labels.instance }} xid bursts'
```

This avoids firing on single one-offs.

leo: :thumbsup: Increasing the window to 5m and adding a `for` helps. Also add labels for `driver_version` and `node` to help triage.

derek: One gotcha: counters reset on exporter restarts or driver events — use `increase()` but also guard against wrap/resets (clamp_min or check scrape times).

sasha: We should also consider hysteresis: if node sees bursts across multiple GPUs over 30m, tag for quarantine/drain rather than per-card immediate drain. That reduces churn during maintenance windows.

maria: Another draft rule using ratio and longer window — still permissive but less noisy:

```yaml
- alert: GPUCardXidAdaptive
  expr: |
    sum by(instance,gpu) (increase(dcgm_gpu_xid_errors_total[10m])) 
      / max(1, sum by(instance,gpu) (increase(dcgm_gpu_total_ops[10m]))) > 0.01
  for: 15m
  labels:
    severity: major
  annotations:
    runbook: /runbooks/gpu-xid-triage
```

Pair this with recording rules to precompute the ratios and a rolling z-score for outlier detection.

oncall-bot: Incident bot: new alert group GPUCardXidAdaptive fired at 2766666200, routed to oncall.

leo: I like precomputing the ratios in recording rules to keep Prom eval cheap. Avoid expensive per-eval math in the alert expr.

derek: Triage checklist idea: 1) check dcgm exporter logs, 2) dmesg for resets, 3) nvidia-smi -q ECC counts, 4) compare driver version + kernel updates, 5) if persistent -> drain + RMA.

sasha: I'll prototype the recording rules + Grafana panel showing 10m vs 30m deltas per card. Will open a PR with tests (promtool) tomorrow.

maria: I'll also open an RFC PR with the proposed rules + synthetic workload tests. Suggest we can roll to canary region (eus1) then usw2.

oncall-bot: Deploy bot: prometheus/rules/gpu-adaptive-windowing.yaml pushed to staging at 2766666299
